transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora. I've completed your post-cataract surgery follow-up check today. 

Do you have any questions about your surgery or your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Yes, I do have a few questions. When can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a great question! You should avoid any exercise for the first week after surgery. After that week, you can go back to light exercise like gardening, brisk walking, or light jogging. Just avoid any strenuous or heavy exercise for about a month.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for the information. Yes, I have another question. When can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question. If you were using eye drops or gel for dry eyes before your operation, it's safe to continue using them unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

However, if you're not sure about the specific product you have, I'd recommend checking with your GP or pharmacist to confirm it's okay to use.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for clarifying that. I do have another question. I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Yes, some light sensitivity is normal as your eyes adjust to the new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to assess it further. In that case, please contact your care team.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks, that makes sense. I have one more question. Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's quite common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after surgery, and it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

However, I don't have your specific details, so I'm not sure exactly how long it's been since your operation. If your vision is still blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything is okay. 

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Nope, I don't have any more questions. Thanks for answering them all!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Brilliant! So just to confirm - have all your questions about your cataract surgery recovery been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, they have. Thank you for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! Take care, and best wishes with your recovery.

verdict.label: pass

All points were covered.
